paper_metadata.title: Intracranial hemorrhage in a large cohort of patients supported with veno-venous ECMO. A retrospective single-center analysis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study describes a large consecutive cohort from a single center with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, there is significant selection bias potential because 159 patients (22% of the eligible cohort) were excluded solely due to the lack of cerebral imaging, which the authors admit may have led to missed subclinical ICB cases.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: We used the ECMO database of the University Hospital Regensburg (UKR) for this retrospective analysis. The database records important clinical information on all ECMO patients (patient-related data, ECMO characteristics, ventilator settings, medication, hemodynamic data, laboratory values and complications).
items.reasoning: The source is a specific university hospital database covering all ECMO patients with comprehensive clinical data points listed.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: All consecutive patients supported with V-V ECMO at the UKR between December 2006 and March 2019 were eligible for this analysis.
items.reasoning: The study uses a consecutive sampling method over a defined 13-year period, which is the gold standard for reducing selection bias in retrospective cohorts.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between December 2006 and March 2019
items.reasoning: The start and end dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: University Hospital Regensburg (UKR)
items.reasoning: The specific tertiary care center and location are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: All patients included met the following inclusion criteria: availability of at least one cerebral imaging (cerebral computed tomography (cCT) or cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (cMRI)) obtained during or after ECMO support. Patients were excluded if there was evidence of cerebral bleeding prior to ECMO or ICB due to trauma.
items.reasoning: Criteria are clearly defined, including the requirement for imaging and specific exclusion of pre-existing or traumatic bleeds.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Among 722 patients (739 V-V ECMO runs) during the study period, 182 runs did not meet the inclusion criteria due to: (a) no cerebral imaging obtained during ECMO support (159 runs)
items.reasoning: While the study captures a large number, the exclusion of 159 patients (approx 22%) due to lack of imaging creates a 'convenience' subset of those stable enough or clinically indicated for imaging, potentially biasing the incidence and risk factor associations.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Baseline characteristics and laboratory values before the start of V-V ECMO treatment are shown in Table 1.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides extensive baseline data including age, sex, SOFA score, indication, and various laboratory/ventilator parameters.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: As a retrospective database study focused on in-hospital outcomes (ICB detection and hospital discharge), the 'attrition' is essentially zero for the primary endpoint. The flow of patients is well-accounted for.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis

items.evidence_snippet: In total, 556 patients were included in the analysis (Figure 1).
items.reasoning: The study analyzes the full cohort of patients who met the inclusion criteria through to hospital discharge or death.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (platelets, paCO2, etc.) were measured using standard laboratory and blood gas techniques. The timing (pre-ECMO and 2h post) is clearly defined and consistent for the cohort.

items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: All patients undergo arterial blood gas analysis (ABG) before V-V ECMO cannulation (pre-ECMO values) and 2 h after initiation. Each morning... hematological, biochemical, and coagulative blood markers are recorded.
items.reasoning: The PFs are standard clinical lab values with clear timing of measurement.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF

items.reasoning: Standardized hospital laboratory and ABG machines provide high reliability and validity.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: To calculate ORs, variables were dichotomized using the ICB group median before V-V ECMO as the cut-off point.
items.reasoning: The use of the 'ICB group median' as a cut-off is data-dependent, which can lead to overestimation of effect sizes compared to pre-specified clinical thresholds.

items.evidence_snippet: The standard of care at our institution is... aPTT and dose of UFH/argatroban are monitored and adjusted daily
items.reasoning: Measurements were part of a standardized institutional protocol for all ECMO patients.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the definition of ICB is clear and based on imaging, the lack of a systematic screening protocol for all patients (and the exclusion of those without imaging) introduces a risk that the 'outcome' was not measured identically or at the same frequency for all participants.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Formal radiologists' description and reports of cerebral imaging were screened to identify evidence of cerebral pathology, namely: intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, subdural hemorrhage, or epidural hemorrhage.
items.reasoning: The outcome (ICB) is clearly defined by radiological subtypes.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Reports describing ICB were reviewed and reevaluated in collaboration with a radiologist.
items.reasoning: The use of CT/MRI and expert re-evaluation by a radiologist ensures high validity.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: screening was performed, but no systematic or standardized protocol was used... 159 ECMO runs... were excluded due to missing cerebral imaging.
items.reasoning: The authors admit the lack of a standardized protocol. Some patients were screened early, others only upon clinical suspicion, and many were excluded entirely because they never received imaging.

items.reasoning: The study measured a wide array of clinical and laboratory variables known to influence ICB risk.

items.evidence_snippet: Impaired kidney function before ECMO was defined as a creatinine level higher than 1.5 mg/dl. KDIGO criteria defined acute kidney failure.
items.reasoning: Definitions for key confounders like renal failure are provided.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are standard and well-described. The use of AIC for model selection and adherence to TRIPOD guidelines suggests a robust analytical approach, despite the exploratory nature of the study.

items.reasoning: The strategy for moving from univariate to multivariable modeling is clearly explained.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: The multivariable regression model included all factors with a p-value < 0.1 in the univariable analysis. According to the TRIPOD Statement, assumed risk factors were not predefined in this exploratory analysis.
items.reasoning: The strategy is transparent and follows established reporting guidelines (TRIPOD) for exploratory prognostic studies.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
